mitigations.name: Control/Data Flow Separation
mitigations.description: Architectural defense that creates a protective system layer around LLMs by explicitly separating control flow (from trusted queries) from data flow (including untrusted tool descriptions). Ensures malicious instructions embedded in data cannot influence program execution. The most notable implementation is CaMeL (Control and Memory Language), developed by Google researchers, demonstrating 77% task completion with provable security guarantees.
corePrinciples: Explicit Control Flow Extraction: Parse and extract control flow from trusted sources only
Data Isolation: Treat all external inputs as pure data
Capability-Based Security: Implement fine-grained permissions for data access and flow
benefits: Provable Security: Mathematical guarantees against certain attack classes
Defense in Depth: Works even if underlying LLM is vulnerable
No Model Retraining: Can be applied to existing LLMs
limitations: Performance Impact: ~7% reduction in task completion rate
Not Universal: Some tasks may be incompatible with strict separation
references: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design - Google Research (2025) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813

mitigations.name: Cryptographic Integrity for Tool Descriptions
mitigations.description: Ensures MCP tool descriptions cannot be tampered with by implementing digital signatures and hash verification. Tool descriptions are signed by trusted authorities, and clients verify signatures before loading any tool, preventing unauthorized modifications at any point in the supply chain.
implementationPhases: Phase 1: Infrastructure Setup - Deploy CA or use existing PKI, create key management procedures, set up secure key storage (HSM recommended)
Phase 2: Tool Signing - Implement signing tools for developers, create CI/CD integration for automated signing
Phase 3: Client Verification - Update MCP clients to require signatures, implement signature verification
Phase 4: Monitoring - Log all signature verifications, alert on verification failures

do: Use hardware security modules (HSM) for private keys
Implement certificate pinning for critical tools
Verify entire tool schema, not just descriptions
Include version information in signed content
Use timestamp servers to prove signing time
dont: Store private keys in version control

references: NIST SP 800-204D: Software Supply Chain Security in DevSecOps
in-toto: Framework for Supply Chain Integrity

mitigations.name: AI-Powered Content Analysis
mitigations.description: Uses specialized LLMs or fine-tuned models to analyze tool descriptions and other inputs for semantic anomalies, hidden instructions, and potential prompt injection attempts before they reach production systems. Can detect novel attack patterns that signature-based systems miss.
implementationApproaches: Dedicated Security LLM: Isolated model specifically for security analysis with risk scoring
Ensemble Approach: Multiple specialized detectors (prompt injection, semantic anomaly, hidden instruction, Unicode abuse)
Fine-tuned Detection Model: Binary classifier trained on labeled safe/malicious examples
detectionPatterns: Semantic Analysis: Contradiction detection, role confusion, capability mismatch
Structural Analysis: Unusual formatting, hidden sections, complexity mismatches
Behavioral Prediction: Predict likely LLM behavior, identify control flow hijacking
limitations: False Positives: May flag legitimate complex descriptions
Computational Cost: Requires additional LLM inference
Adversarial Robustness: Attackers may craft inputs to evade detection
Context Loss: Analyzes descriptions in isolation
Model Drift: Requires regular updates as attack patterns evolve
references: Attention Tracker: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs (2024)

mitigations.name: Unicode Sanitization and Filtering
mitigations.description: Removes or normalizes potentially malicious Unicode characters from tool descriptions and other inputs before they reach LLMs. Filters invisible characters, bidirectional control characters, and characters from Private Use Areas that attackers use to hide malicious instructions.
sanitizationModes: Normalize: Replace with visible markers for debugging
Log-only: Detect and log but don't modify
limitations: Some attacks use allowed characters creatively

mitigations.name: Content Sanitization
mitigations.description: Filters MCP-related content (tool descriptions, tool outputs, error messages, and other data) to remove hidden content and instruction patterns using pattern-based detection combined with structural analysis. Note: pattern-based filtering alone is insufficient and should be combined with other mitigations.

mitigations.name: Tool Registry Verification
mitigations.description: Ensures MCP servers are only installed from verified sources with cryptographic signatures, implementing a trusted registry system similar to package managers like npm or Docker Hub.
references: SLSA Supply Chain Security Framework - https://slsa.dev/

mitigations.name: Content Rendering Parity
mitigations.description: Ensures displayed content matches content sent to the LLM, preventing attackers from hiding malicious instructions that are invisible to users but processed by the model.

mitigations.name: Visual Validation
mitigations.description: Compare visual rendering of descriptions with actual content to detect invisible characters. Helps identify Unicode-based injection attempts.
references: Promptfoo Research on invisible Unicode threats

mitigations.name: Sandboxed Testing
mitigations.description: Test new MCP tools in isolated environments with comprehensive monitoring before production deployment, allowing detection of malicious behavior without risk to production systems.
references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 - SC-39: Process Isolation

mitigations.name: Automated Scanning
mitigations.description: Regularly scan tool descriptions for known malicious patterns and hidden content using automated tools.

mitigations.name: Behavioral Monitoring
mitigations.description: Tracks LLM behavior patterns to detect unexpected tool usage, suspicious sequences of operations, or deviations from normal behavior that may indicate compromise or attack. Includes monitoring for prompt injection signs such as sudden context switches, execution of unrelated commands, or acknowledgment of instructions not visible in the original user request.
references: Large Language Models for Forecasting and Anomaly Detection (2024)
MITRE - Finding Cyber Threats with ATT&CK-Based Analytics

mitigations.name: Audit Logging
mitigations.description: Log all tool descriptions loaded and their full content, along with all tool invocations, parameters, and results for forensic analysis and anomaly detection.

mitigations.name: OAuth Flow Verification
mitigations.description: Implement protocol-level verification of OAuth authorization servers and callback URLs to prevent OAuth phishing attacks through malicious MCP servers. Includes RFC 9207 Authorization Server Issuer Identification validation.
references: RFC 9207 - OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Issuer Identification
OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice - IETF Draft

mitigations.name: Server Allowlisting
mitigations.description: Maintain and enforce a list of trusted MCP server domains to prevent connections to malicious servers. Reject OAuth flows to non-allowlisted domains regardless of configuration.

mitigations.name: User Warning Systems
mitigations.description: Display clear warnings when OAuth flows are initiated, showing the requesting server and target service. Show full URL with visual indicators for security-critical characters.

mitigations.name: Token Scope Limiting
mitigations.description: Enforce minimal OAuth scopes and warn on broad permission requests. Follow principle of least privilege for token permissions.

mitigations.name: Callback URL Restrictions
mitigations.description: Validate that OAuth callback URLs match the configured MCP server domain. Enforce strict redirect URI matching and reject wildcards and open redirects.

mitigations.name: OAuth Flow Monitoring
mitigations.description: Log and analyze all OAuth authorization attempts through MCP, including full URLs, issuer parameters, and certificate details.

mitigations.name: Token Usage Tracking
mitigations.description: Monitor usage patterns of OAuth tokens obtained through MCP to identify potentially compromised tokens.

mitigations.name: Anomaly Detection
mitigations.description: Deploy behavioral analytics to detect unusual OAuth patterns such as first-seen domains, geographic anomalies, or multiple AS configurations. Identify unusual patterns in OAuth requests across MCP servers.

mitigations.name: Output Context Isolation
mitigations.description: Isolate tool output contexts to prevent cross-contamination between tool results and system instructions.

mitigations.name: Semantic Output Validation
mitigations.description: Validate tool outputs for semantic consistency and hidden instructions before they are processed by the LLM.

mitigations.name: Tool Output Truncation
mitigations.description: Truncate tool outputs to prevent oversized payloads from being processed, reducing the attack surface for output-based injection.

mitigations.name: SBOM Generation and Verification
mitigations.description: Generate and verify Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for MCP packages and dependencies to maintain comprehensive inventory and detect unauthorized components.

mitigations.name: AI-Specific Risk Modeling
mitigations.description: Model AI-specific risks in MCP deployments, incorporating threat modeling tailored to LLM and agent-based systems.

mitigations.name: Data Provenance Tracking
mitigations.description: Track and verify the provenance of data flowing through MCP tools to ensure data integrity and detect unauthorized modifications.

mitigations.name: Social Engineering Awareness Training
mitigations.description: Train users to recognize social engineering attacks targeting MCP installations, including phishing attempts to install malicious MCP servers.

mitigations.name: Pre-Authentication Tool Concealment
mitigations.description: Conceal tool capabilities until proper authentication is established, preventing unauthorized tool discovery and enumeration.

mitigations.name: Explicit Privilege Boundaries
mitigations.description: Define and enforce explicit privilege boundaries for MCP tools and servers, limiting blast radius if a spoofed or compromised endpoint is accepted.

mitigations.name: Vector Store Integrity Verification
mitigations.description: Cryptographically verify the integrity of vector store contents to detect unauthorized modifications or contamination of long-term AI agent memory.

mitigations.name: OAuth Token Validation
mitigations.description: Validate OAuth tokens with improved code quality and type safety to prevent token-based attacks.

mitigations.name: Continuous Vector Store Monitoring
mitigations.description: Continuously monitor vector stores for contamination and unauthorized modifications that could affect AI agent behavior across sessions.

mitigations.name: Training Data Provenance Verification
mitigations.description: Verify the provenance and integrity of training data used for AI models in MCP tools to prevent training data poisoning attacks.

mitigations.name: AI Model Integrity Validation
mitigations.description: Validate AI model integrity through cryptographic checksums and signatures to detect tampering or unauthorized model replacement.

mitigations.name: Adversarial Training Data Detection
mitigations.description: Detect adversarial manipulations in training data using AI-based analysis to identify poisoned samples before they affect model behavior.

mitigations.name: Model Behavior Monitoring
mitigations.description: Monitor AI model behavior for deviations indicating poisoning or compromise, including statistical analysis of model outputs over time.

mitigations.name: Metadata Sanitization
mitigations.description: Sanitize tool metadata to remove or flag suspicious properties that could be used for defense evasion or manipulation attacks.

mitigations.name: Schema Validation
mitigations.description: Validate tool schemas against expected patterns and structures to detect anomalies or malicious modifications.

mitigations.name: Prompt Context Validation
mitigations.description: Validate prompt context integrity before processing to detect context manipulation or injection attempts.

mitigations.name: Clear UI Patterns
mitigations.description: Implement clear UI patterns to help users identify security-relevant actions, reducing consent fatigue and improving user awareness of risks.

mitigations.name: Tool and Package Pinning
mitigations.description: Pin tool and package versions to prevent unauthorized updates, protecting against rug pull attacks and supply chain compromise via auto-update mechanisms.

mitigations.name: Cross-Server Protection
mitigations.description: Implement protections against cross-server attacks and tool interference, ensuring tool isolation between different MCP server instances.

mitigations.name: Steganography Scanner
mitigations.description: Scan for steganographic content in tool descriptions and outputs, including zero-width characters, HTML comments, and other encoding techniques used to hide malicious instructions.

mitigations.name: Behavioural Monitoring
mitigations.description: Advanced behavioral monitoring specifically for MCP tool and server activities, complementing general behavioral monitoring with MCP-specific patterns.

mitigations.name: Tool Manifest Signing & Server Attestation
mitigations.description: Validate server identity and manifest integrity before accepting tools. Combines cryptographic signing of tool manifests with server attestation to ensure both the server and its tools are authentic.

mitigations.name: Bridge Risk Management
mitigations.description: Manage risks associated with cross-chain bridge operations, including monitoring bridge contracts, validating cross-chain messages, and implementing rate limits on transfers.

mitigations.name: Cross-Chain Transaction Graph Analysis
mitigations.description: Analyze cross-chain transaction graphs for suspicious patterns indicative of laundering or asset obfuscation through bridges and DEXs.

mitigations.name: Custodial Off-Ramp Monitoring
mitigations.description: Monitor custodial off-ramp activities for suspicious transactions that may indicate laundered or stolen funds being converted to fiat currency.

mitigations.name: Multimodal Input Scanning
mitigations.description: Scan multimodal inputs (images, audio) for embedded malicious instructions before they are processed by multimodal AI models.

mitigations.name: Multimodal Content Isolation
mitigations.description: Isolate multimodal content processing from instruction execution to prevent cross-modal prompt injection attacks.

mitigations.name: Embedding Anomaly Detection
mitigations.description: Detect anomalies in embedding patterns that may indicate tool shadowing, content injection, or other manipulation attempts.

mitigations.name: Input Validation Pipeline
mitigations.description: Multi-stage input validation pipeline for comprehensive threat detection across all input types and modalities. Validates tool descriptions and metadata for suspicious patterns before registration.

mitigations.name: Multimodal Watermarking
mitigations.description: Apply watermarking to multimodal content for provenance tracking and tamper detection.

mitigations.name: Cross-Modal Consistency Check
mitigations.description: Verify consistency between different modalities (text, image, audio) to detect injection attempts where malicious content is hidden in one modality.

mitigations.name: Technique Name Standardization
mitigations.description: Standardize technique naming conventions for consistent reference across the framework and organizational documentation.

mitigations.name: Out-of-Band Authorization for Privileged Tool Invocations
mitigations.description: Out-of-Band Authorization for Privileged Tool Invocations is a host-side control that requires every call to a privileged MCP tool to pass through an authorization step whose decision is made and enforced outside the model's context window.

mitigations.name: Tool-Invocation Anomaly Detection & Baselining
mitigations.description: Tool-Invocation Anomaly Detection & Baselining is a detective control that profiles per-agent, per-user, per-tool baselines of MCP tool-call behavior and raises alerts when live invocations deviate from those baselines along one or more feature dimensions.

mitigations.name: Query Guardrails & Result Limits
mitigations.description: Query Guardrails & Result Limits is a preventive control for MCP tools that execute queries against databases, data warehouses, or other structured stores.

mitigations.name: Data Loss Prevention on Tool Outputs
mitigations.description: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) on Tool Outputs applies column-level classification, masking, tokenization, and sensitive-content detection to the results returned by MCP tools before those results enter the agent's context window or are surfaced to a user.

mitigations.name: Sampling Budget and Iteration Caps
mitigations.description: Sampling Budget and Iteration Caps enforces hard, client-side limits on how much nested model work an MCP server can trigger through sampling/createMessage during a single user-intent flow or session.

mitigations.name: Per-Invocation Capability Brokering
mitigations.description: Per-Invocation Capability Brokering interposes a supervisor between an MCP server and the host OS for every individual tool call.

defenseInDepth: Foundation Layer: Implement architectural defenses (SAFE-M-1, SAFE-M-21) that provide fundamental protection
Prevention Layer: Add cryptographic controls (SAFE-M-2) and input validation (SAFE-M-4, SAFE-M-5, SAFE-M-22)
Detection Layer: Deploy monitoring and detection controls (SAFE-M-10, SAFE-M-11, SAFE-M-12)
Response Layer: Maintain audit logs and incident response procedures

additional.label: Implement as Resources Allow
additional.description: Remaining mitigations based on specific threat model
